Hypotheses:
- nda-11: No reverse engineering | Receiving Party shall not reverse engineer any objects which embody Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
- nda-16: Return of confidential information | Receiving Party shall destroy or return some Confidential Information upon the termination of Agreement.
- nda-15: No licensing | Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information.
- nda-10: Confidentiality of Agreement | Receiving Party shall not disclose the fact that Agreement was agreed or negotiated.
- nda-2: None-inclusion of non-technical information | Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
- nda-1: Explicit identification | All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party.
- nda-19: Survival of obligations | Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement.
- nda-12: Permissible development of similar information | Receiving Party may independently develop information similar to Confidential Information.
- nda-20: Permissible post-agreement possession | Receiving Party may retain some Confidential Information even after the return or destruction of Confidential Information.
- nda-3: Inclusion of verbally conveyed information | Confidential Information may include verbally conveyed information.
- nda-18: No solicitation | Receiving Party shall not solicit some of Disclosing Party's representatives.
- nda-7: Sharing with third-parties | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some third-parties (including consultants, agents and professional advisors).
- nda-17: Permissible copy | Receiving Party may create a copy of some Confidential Information in some circumstances.
- nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure | Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or judicial process to disclose any Confidential Information.
- nda-13: Permissible acquirement of similar information | Receiving Party may acquire information similar to Confidential Information from a third party.
- nda-5: Sharing with employees | Receiving Party may share some Confidential Information with some of Receiving Party's employees.
- nda-4: Limited use | Receiving Party shall not use any Confidential Information for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement.

Thought: Let me analyze each hypothesis against the document segments.

- nda-11 (No reverse engineering): Not mentioned in the document. → NotMentioned
- nda-16 (Return of confidential information): No clause about returning/destroying CI upon termination. → NotMentioned
- nda-15 (No licensing): No clause stating agreement grants no rights. → NotMentioned (though [7] grants access, there's no explicit no-license clause)
- nda-10 (Confidentiality of Agreement): No clause about not disclosing the agreement's existence. → NotMentioned
- nda-2 (None-inclusion of non-technical info): [3] lists CI including "services, customers etc" — this includes non-technical information, contradicting "only technical information". → Contradiction, evidence [3]
- nda-1 (Explicit identification): [7] says CI "as identified and reduced in writing or provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing" — this means CI need not be expressly identified; verbal/unwritten disclosure allowed. This contradicts "All CI shall be expressly identified". → Contradiction, evidence [7]
- nda-19 (Survival of obligations): [29] term continues until termination; no survival clause. → NotMentioned
- nda-12 (Permissible development of similar info): Not mentioned. → NotMentioned
- nda-20 (Permissible post-agreement possession): Not mentioned. → NotMentioned
- nda-3 (Inclusion of verbally conveyed information): [7] "provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing" → Entailment, evidence [7]
- nda-18 (No solicitation): Not mentioned. → NotMentioned
- nda-7 (Sharing with third-parties): [10] says not to share with any Third Party; no permission. → NotMentioned (or Contradiction? The hypothesis says "may share" — document says no sharing at all, no exception. So there's no permission; hypothesis is contradicted? Typically in these tasks, if the document prohibits sharing entirely without exceptions, the hypothesis "may share some CI with some third-parties" is contradicted by [10]. Hmm. [10]: "Recipient agrees not to use the Confidential Information in any way or under any circumstances share the same... with any Third Party." This directly contradicts permissible sharing. → Contradiction, evidence [10]. But careful: contradiction requires the hypothesis to be false given the text. "May share some CI with some third-parties" — the text prohibits all sharing with third parties, so this is contradicted. → Contradiction [10]
- nda-17 (Permissible copy): Not mentioned explicitly. [15] access to layout plan — not copying. → NotMentioned
- nda-8 (Notice on compelled disclosure): [11] says Recipient must prevent disclosure even if authorized/directed under law, without express permission of Discloser. This implies needing Discloser's permission, but not exactly "notify". The hypothesis: "shall notify Disclosing Party in case required by law to disclose". [11] requires express permission of Discloser before any legally-directed disclosure — this entails involving/notifying the Discloser. Many NDA datasets label this as Entailment with evidence [11]. The requirement to obtain express permission implies notification. → Entailment, evidence [11]
- nda-13 (Permissible acquirement of similar info): Not mentioned. → NotMentioned
- nda-5 (Sharing with employees): Not mentioned. → NotMentioned
- nda-4 (Limited use): [10] "Recipient agrees not to use the Confidential Information in any way" — combined with [5] purpose. Actually [10] says not to use in any way or share. Hmm, [10] says no use at all. The hypothesis: shall not use CI for any purpose other than purposes stated. [5] states the Purpose; [7] grants access. [15] access to layout plan for purpose of carrying out contract. The document restricts use to purpose implicitly. [10] "not to use the Confidential Information in any way" is even stricter. Does it entail limited use? If no use at all is allowed except access for the Purpose, then yes — use limited to stated purpose is entailed. Evidence [10] (and [5]). I'd say Entailment with [10] (and maybe [5]). Let me verify with human_feedback for the key uncertain ones: nda-8, nda-4, nda-7, nda-1, nda-2.
